ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/streaming/generate (prod-usw2). Rule: continuous-batcher-tail-p99 > 3s. Current p95=720ms p99=3.6s, error rate stable. Pager created. thread_ts=3269004567

Kai Chen: saw the alert, I'm on it. grabbing dashboards now.

Maria Lopez: thanks Kai. quick customer check: any 1p customers routed to this cluster? -> Looks like multiple mid-market tenants, one with high streaming traffic (acme-marketing) on dedicated route but using shared batcher.

Samir Patel: initial hypothesis: continuous-batching scheduler fairness + mixed sequence lengths causing long wait for short-streaming calls. We've had similar behavior when packer greedily waits to fill batches.

Kai Chen: confirmed from trace sample: streaming requests with short prompt (20-50 tokens) are getting packed into large batch windows waiting for long sequences. KV cache churn low. I see packer queue depth high. snippet from trace: 
```
request_id=rid-8a7f
seq_len=28
queued_ms=1450
batch_size=96
serving_ms=2100
```

ops-bot: added runbook reference: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/contbatch-tail (see section 2).

Maria Lopez: customer impact: Acme streaming saw UI stalls and slower token streaming; some user sessions timed out at 5s. Product wants customer-notify decision.

Samir Patel: mitigation options (fast -> slow):
- reduce max_batch_size on packer for streaming route to 32 (cheap, immediate)
- enable preemptive packing for streaming requests (forces small seqs ahead)
- lower pack wait_timeout from 50ms -> 20ms for routes tagged streaming
- route streaming requests to a streaming-priority pool (if capacity)
- fall back to quantized smaller model variant as last resort

Kai Chen: let's do quick config change: reduce max_batch_size to 32 on the affected pool and lower wait_timeout to 25ms. I'll patch config and rollout to one shard first. doing now.

Kai Chen: patch applied to shard-3. Monitoring.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: config-change applied by kai at 3269004670 to cluster-prod-usw2/shard-3 (max_batch_size=32 wait_timeout_ms=25).

Samir Patel: good. watch for p95/p99. Also check scheduling fairness metrics (fairness_ratio) to ensure we aren't starving long sequences.

Kai Chen: shard-3 p95 dropped from 720ms -> 260ms within 20s. p99 dropped from 3.6s -> 980ms. Streaming stalls reduced in sample traces.

Maria Lopez: prod telemetry shows reduced tail on shard-3. however overall cluster p99 still at ~1.5s because other shards not patched.

Ryan O'Neill: I can take the rollout to remaining shards. plan: rollout to 4 shards every 30s with canary checks for error rate and p99. if anything regresses rollback.

Kai Chen: agree. checklist for rollout: 
- apply config to next shard
- wait 30s -> check p95/p99 & error rate
- if p99 > previous by 50% or errors increase, rollback
- note customer impact time window for notify

Samir Patel: also schedule a follow-up engineering task: improve packer heuristics to prefer small seqs for streaming tag, and add an adaptive threshold based on current seq_len distribution. Will file ticket after live mitigation.

Kai Chen: rollout in progress. shard-4 -> applied at 3269004755.

ops-bot: monitor: cluster p95=280ms p99=1.1s. overall request rates unchanged.

Maria Lopez: I'm drafting a short customer blurb for Acme: "We observed intermittent streaming stalls impacting token delivery latency. We mitigated by adjusting batching configuration; streaming experience is restored. No data loss." ping me if we need to expand.

Samir Patel: note: this config change increases per-token GPU cost slightly due to smaller batches. Ops: please track cost delta. We'll revert to smarter packer later to recover cost.

Ryan O'Neill: continuing rollout, shards 5-8 applied. At shard-8 now p99 across cluster stabilized at ~900ms.

Kai Chen: leaving a short postmortem stub: cause = continuous packer waiting for mixed-length sequences; short streaming requests starved and got placed into large batches, increasing queuing. immediate mitigation = reduce max_batch_size + shorten wait_timeout + staged rollout. follow-ups = scheduler fairness fix, adaptive batching by seq distribution, per-route streaming priority pool.

Maria Lopez: agree. Customer notify sent (screenshot of message saved).

Ryan O'Neill: handing off to next oncall (Ryan -> Samir) for 3h watch. Samir, take over monitoring and follow-up ticketing.\nSamir Patel: taking handoff. I'll watch p99 for next 3 hours, check cost delta, and open a ticket for packer heuristic work (ENG-5241).

Kai Chen: logging summary for postmortem:
- start 3269004567 ops-bot alert
- mitigation start 3269004670 (shard-3 config)
- cluster stable 3269004830
- handoff 3269004870 Samir 3h watch

ops-bot: incident closed by Kai (temporary mitigations applied). Please file postmortem within 48h.

Maria Lopez: thanks team. good run. :thumbsup:
